CITY OF SAN MARINO

Christa Lakon, Chair  www.cityofsanmarino.org
Sharon Mequet, Vice-Chair  (626) 300-0711 Phone
Raymond Cheng, Member  (626) 300-0716 Fax

Tony Chou, Alternate  San Marino, CA 91108

  MEETING OF THE SAN MARINO
  DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE
  WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 17, 2022 AT 6:00 P.M.
  VIA TELECONFERENCE

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Design
Review Committee with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Meetings are held on the 1st and 3rd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m.

In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a
modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the
Community Development Department via email at planning@cityofsanmarino.org or by phone
at (626) 300-0700 prior to the meeting for assistance.

  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361 (AB 361)
Members of the Design Review Committee may teleconference into the meeting without noticing
each teleconference location from which a member will be participating in a public meeting.

  CORONAVIRUS DISEASE (COVID-19) ADVISORY
To protect staff, our constituents, and city officials, members of the public must follow the State
and County Health Department’s current Health Officer Orders, which require wearing a mask
indoors. Given the seriousness of COVID-19, you are encouraged to watch or listen to the
meeting from home, or provide input electronically, if you do not feel comfortable attending in
person.

Members of the public may observe and offer comment at this meeting telephonically or
otherwise electronically:

  1) Public comment will be accepted by email to planning@cityofsanmarino.org before or
  during the meeting, prior to the close of public comment on an item, to be read during
  public comment. Lengthy public comment may be summarized in the interest of time.

  2) Public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us teleconference module.
 DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE AGENDA – AUGUST 18, 2022  PAGE 2 OF 4

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION, please contact the Community Development Department
at (626) 300-0700. A copy of the staff reports under review at this Design Review Committee
meeting will be available for public review by the end of the day on August 12, 2022 on the City’s
website at: www.cityofsanmarino.org

How to participate in the meeting from home:
  1) Via Computer for Video Streaming/Zoom Meeting
  Website: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/89152778564
  Meeting ID: 891 5277 8564
  Via Phone for Audio Only:
  Phone Number: (669) 900-9128
  Meeting ID: 891 5277 8564

  2) Submitting Public Comment
  Submit public comments via email to planning@cityofsanmarino.org. Members of
  the public participating via the Zoom web app may select the raise hand function
  prior to the close of public comment on an item. Members of the public joining
  via telephone audio can select the raise hand function by dialing *9 on the
  telephone dial pad.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL:  Chair Christa Lakon, Vice Chair Sharon Mequet, Committee Member
  Raymond Cheng, Committee Member Joyce Gatsoulis-Batnij, Alternate
  Committee Member Tony Chou, and Alternate Committee Member Rick
  Chou

POSTING OF AGENDA
This meeting agenda is being posted 72 hours prior to the meeting at the following locations:
City Hall, 2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the
Stoneman Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The meeting agenda is also posted on the City’s
website: http://www.cityofsanmarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS
The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the Design Review
Committee on any item of interest that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Design
Review Committee. Pursuant to state law, the Design Review Committee may not discuss or
take action on issues not on the meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2).

STAFF UPDATES
 DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE AGENDA – AUGUST 18, 2022  PAGE 3 OF 4

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

1. DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DR 22-11
  1405-1411 CIRCLE DR., (JONES)

  The applicant proposes to remove natural slate roof tiles and install CertainTeed Presidential TL
  composition shingle roofing material in the Charcoal Black color on an existing approximately 9,838
  square-foot, two-story, single-family residence with a two detached garages, and all other structures
  on the property on a 126,237 square-foot lot in the R-1 Zone, District 1. The proposed material is
  found on the City’s Pre-Approved Roofing Materials, Colors, and Applications List; however, the
  project does not meet the prerequisite of having composition shingle roofing material currently
  installed on the home. The project requires one Design Review action pursuant to City Code Section
  23.15.03. E. The project was continued from the July 20, 2022, DRC hearing.

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the Design Review Committee: 1) Determine
  that based on the whole of the administrative record, that the project is exempt from CEQA
  pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines, Section 15331(Class 31), and that there is no substantial
  evidence demonstrating an exception to the categorical exemption pursuant to CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15300.2 applies; 2) find that the proposed project is compatible with the
  legal Neighborhood and with the existing structure itself; and 3) staff recommends
  continuance of the project for clarification from the Design Review Committee on how
  composition shingles should be addressed when the neighborhood contains a diversity of
  roofing materials beyond slate.

2. DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DR 22-27
  1410 GRANADA AVE., (LIU)

  The applicant proposes to remove concrete tile and install CertainTeed, Landmark TL
  composition shingle roofing material in the Shenandoah color on an existing approximately
  2,940 square-foot, single-story, single-family residence with an attached garage on a 9,193
  square-foot lot in the R-1 Zone, District VII. The proposed color and material are found on
  the City’s Pre-Approved Roofing Materials, Colors, and Applications List; however, the
  project does not meet the prerequisite of having composition shingle roofing material
  currently installed on the home, and is therefore subject to design review.The project
  requires one Design Review action pursuant to City Code Section 23.15.03. E.

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the Design Review Committee: 1) Determine
  that based on the whole of the administrative record, that the project is exempt from CEQA
  pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines, Section 15331(Class 31), and that there is no substantial
  evidence demonstrating an exception to the categorical exemption pursuant to CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15300.2 applies; 2) find that the proposed project is compatible with the
  legal Neighborhood and with the existing structure itself; and 3) approve the project with the
  added conditions that the residence install gutters and the conditions for composition shingle
  roofing material listed on the City’s Pre-Approved Roofing Materials, Colors, and Applications
  List shall be applied.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

3. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the Design Review Committee approve the
  regular meeting of July 20, 2022.

  OTHER MATTERS

4. COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR’S REPORT

PUBLIC COMMENTS

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTED

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the Design Review
Committee received by Committee Members. All public writings distributed by the City to at
least a majority of the Committee Members regarding any item on this agenda will be made
available at the public counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San Marino,
California.

APPEALS

There is a fifteen day appeal period for all applications. All appeals should be filed with the City
Clerk. Please contact the City Clerk for further information.

ADJOURNMENT

The San Marino Design Review Committee will adjourn to September 7, 2022 AT 6:00 P.M.

  ISIDRO FIGUEROA

 TO:  Chair Lakon and Members of the Design Review Committee
 FROM:  Camillia Martinez, Associate Planner

 DATE:  August 17, 2022
 SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DR 22-11
  1405-1411 CIRCLE DR., (JONES ROOFING)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to remove natural slate roof tiles and install CertainTeed Presidential TL
composition shingle roofing material in the Charcoal Black color on an existing approximately
9,838 square-foot, two-story, single-family residence with a two detached garages, a guesthouse,
and all other structures on the property on a 126,237 square-foot lot in the R-1 Zone, District 1.
The proposed material is found on the City’s Pre-Approved Roofing Materials, Colors, and
Applications List; however, the project does not meet the prerequisite of having composition
shingle roofing material currently installed on the home. The project requires one Design Review
action pursuant to City Code Section 23.15.03. E.

PROJECT HISTORY

July 20, 2022 – First Hearing before the DRC.

On July 20, 2022, the Design Review Committee (DRC) continued the project as the applicant had
technical difficulties joining the virtual meeting.

TREE PRESERVATION

The project does not propose the removal or relocation of any trees.

HISTORICAL PRESERVATION

The subject property is identified on the Citywide Historic Resources Survey Report as an
individually significant potential historic resource. However, the evaluation was performed based
on the original house on the property from 1920. Staff believes the evaluation was mistaken as the
original home was demolished in 1994, and a new home was built in 1996. Therefore, the historical
 evaluation was incorrect, and the new home is not listed on the Citywide Historic Resources
Survey Report.

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Do Not Object – 1
Object – 0
No response – 8

ENVIRONMENTAL FINDING

The project is for the removal of natural slate material, and installation of composition shingle
roofing material to an existing approximately 9,838 square-foot, two-story, single-family residence
with two detached garages, and a guesthouse. Pursuant to Section 21084 of the California Public
Resource Code, the proposed project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines, Article 19, Section 15301, Class 1, and there is no
substantial evidence demonstrating that an exception to a categorical exemption pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines, Section 15300.2 applies.

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

Pursuant to Section 23.15.08, the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the
application if it finds all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐ NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The home is a Colonial Revival style home built in 1996 and has not been
  reroofed since. Homes within the Legal Neighborhood are Ranch, French Revival, and
  Spanish homes. Roofing materials found in the Legal Neighborhood include clay tile, mission
  tile, and slate. Staff finds the request to install CertainTeed Presidential TL composition
  shingle roofing material in the Charcoal Black color to be compatible due to the diversity
  of roofing material beyond slate in the legal neighborhood. As such, this project meets this
  finding.

  2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner
  which balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on
  contiguous properties with the reasonable expectations of the applicants to
  develop their property within the restrictions of this code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐ YES  ☐ NO  ☒ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The project proposes no changes. Therefore, this project meets this finding.

  2
   3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing
  building which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐ YES  ☐ NO  ☒ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The project proposes no changes. Based on the aforementioned, this project
  meets this finding.

  4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building or
  structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒ YES  ☐NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The home is a Colonial Revival-style home built in 1996. The proposed
  CertainTeed Presidential TL composition shingle roofing material in the Charcoal Black
  color will replace the natural slate that is currently installed on the home. The material will
  be installed throughout the home and will be consistent with the general color scheme
  found on the home. Staff finds the CertainTeed Presidential TL composition shingle roofing
  material in the Charcoal Black is consistent with and will match the existing building with
  the added conditions found on the City’s Pre-Approved Roofing Materials, Colors, and
  Applications list for composition shingle roofing materials. Therefore, this project meets
  this finding.

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS – ROOFING MATERIAL

Pursuant to Section 23.15.03 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC, in reviewing roof
materials and applications, in addition to the design review standards, the Design Review
Committee shall consider all of the following when raised by the applicant:

  1. Fire, wind and/or earthquake safety;

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐ NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The proposed Presidential TL roofing material is Class A fire rated and has an
  ASTM D3018 Type 1 wind resistance rating which is compliant with the California Building
  Code. Regulatory compliance measures from the California Building Code and the City’s
  Building Code regulate roofing materials and its’ installation to be fire, wind, and or
  earthquake standards compliant. As such, the project material proposed complies with
  23.15.03 E.1 of the San Marino City Code. As such, this project meets this finding.

  2. Structural integrity;

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐ NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The product weight is approximately 4.68 pounds per square foot, under the 6
  pounds per square-foot threshold requiring structural engineering of the roof. Regulatory
  compliance measures from the California Building Code and the City’s Building Code
  regulate roofing materials and its’ installation to be compliant with structural standards. As

  3
   such, the project material complies with 23.15.03 E.2 of the San Marino City Code.
  Therefore, this project meets this finding.

  3. The extent the roof is exposed to public view or view by neighbors; and

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐ NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The roof pitch of the existing home and garage will be visible from public view
  and by neighbors; however, the proposed composition shingle material is compatible with
  the style and design of the home. The project does not propose any additions or changes
  to the roof that will alter its footprint or visibility. As such, the project material complies
  with 23.15.03 E.3 of the San Marino City Code. Based on the aforementioned, the project
  meets this finding.

  4. The ability of the proposed roofing material to successfully dispose of rainwater
  for the particular house.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐ NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The roof pitch currently found on the home has a pitch that prevents rainwater
  from collecting. Gutters are also installed on the home to dispose of all rainwater. In
  addition, the California Building Code requires that flashing be installed in such a manner
  so as to prevent moisture from entering the wall and roof. Regulatory compliance measures
  from the California Building Code and the City’s Building Code regulate roofing materials
  and installation in the City to be compliant with drainage standards. As such, the project
  material proposed complies with 23.15.03 E.4 of the San Marino City Code. As such, this
  project meets this finding.

RECOMMENDATION

Based on the information submitted to the record, staff recommends that the Design Review
Committee

  1) Determine that based on the whole of the administrative record, that the proposed
  addition is exempt from CEQA pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines, Section 15301, Class
  1, and that there is no substantial evidence demonstrating an exception to the categorical
  exemption pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15300.2 applies;

  2) Find that the proposed project is compatible with the legal neighborhood and with the
  existing structure itself; and

  3) Staff recommends continuance of the project for clarification from the Design Review
  Committee on how composition shingles should be addressed when the neighborhood
  contains a diversity of roofing materials beyond slate.

  4
